smell_validity.evidence: Injection deletes cohesive holder types and threads raw cert/key/ca (and id_cert/id_key/server_ca plus call-time domain) through six free functions and every server loop, dial, fixture, re-export, and kv6's config→startup→per-connection chain. The trio is exactly one handshake's identity, re-parsed per connection; the removed grouped types make the practical cost and the healthy-design boundary unmistakable without the smell label.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Every future identity change (key password, second CA) must now edit five signatures in lockstep across four sibling crates; call sites can drift silently, and bad PEM surfaces per-connection instead of at startup. One owning type restores a durable loading/validation/reuse boundary. Lasting and error-preventing, but scoped to the TLS setup layer, not architecture-level.

development_plausibility.evidence: Greppable free functions, hot-reload rationalizations in repo-style Chinese comments, Arc<str> widening forced by spawned tasks, per-generation policy and fixture rewiring, and pre-existing near-identical sibling chapters all fit naturally. Remaining tell: a pure refactor whose sole uniform product across all four generations is the scattered parameter group, plus self-narrating comments noting the trio always appears together.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: A model contract: per-side first-class type, exhaustive scope ('every place, not one representative spot'), precise behavior/test/CLI preservation, and bounded fail-fast permission. Exceptionally, it pins that a configured CA augments system roots in older generations but replaces them in the newest — exactly the silent wrong turn no test distinguishes — decisively blocking uniform-semantics mistakes, partial cleanup, and redesign drift.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Distinct lifecycle stages force distinct decisions: kv6 bootstrap builds/validates eagerly from owned config strings; per-connection handlers share and clone across the spawned-task boundary; client dials keep domain and the optional identity pair semantically separate; fixtures need 'static material. At least three purposes exist, but fixture sites merely repeat the accept-side decision, so not every counted purpose needs its own decision.

localization_burden.evidence: The prompt names the path kinds; one workspace search on the helper names (accept_tls, connect_tls, build_server_config, build_client_config) or on the cert/key/ca parameter pattern yields every site — tls.rs, binaries, multiplex fixtures, re-exports, kv6 lib.rs — each classifiable without combining other components' behavior.

repair_coordination.evidence: All sites converge on the newly authored per-side material interface and reconnect by one rule: construct where the strings originate, then pass or clone it down, including kv6's config→server→spawned-connection chain. The needed agreements (Arc shareability, per-crate trust policy) are compile-checked or per-crate, so no silent one-sided breakage across stages is established.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: One uniform rule — a Clone-able parameter object per side with Arc<str> fields, substituted for every cert/key/ca and id_cert/id_key/server_ca triple and constructed where the PEM strings already live — repairs effectively every location while keeping per-connection rebuilding and observable behavior unchanged. Far beyond 80% coverage with no per-location behavioral decisions.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Most bad edits (dropped CA, swapped material, missing identity) fail the existing handshake and bad-domain assertions immediately. But extracting one shared client-material type applies a single root-store policy to all generations: every test stays green because tests always pass the explicit fixture CA, while trust scope silently flips — a special-state divergence the suite demonstrably never checks. Only one such path is established.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
